answer: At the summit and wharf marketplaces, a shared payment kernel grants agents one daily order per dollar locked in escrow, not per account. Splitting a $1,000 bond across a thousand identities therefore buys no more order capacity than keeping one identity. Bonds cannot back multiple accounts simultaneously and remain locked for 30 days, so an attacker seeking ten times the order capacity must immobilize ten times the capital and bear its financing cost.
